provenance_note: The reference corpus was authored by another agent from the public specification and the cited standards without access to this code; this run maps each case onto the tool state and recomputes every check from the shipping build through sourceSets(), generate() and solve().
reference: Hand-built functional-test states in the tool-neutral vocabulary of SPEC-functionaltest §13 (rev 2026-09-22.1): the four spec presets (2oo3 SIL 2 trip, five-point loop checks, transfer sequence with retest, trip setpoint revised after FAT), voting-degradation enumeration for 1oo1, 1oo2, 2oo2, 2oo3, 4oo8 and 2oo9 at every coverage level, staleness by FNV-1a hash of the model slice (including the §4.4 worked hashes and the acceptance-4/5 scope of staleness), five-point AI/AO loop arithmetic with boundary cases, DI/DO state checks, SIL proof-test completeness, bypass/force restoration, execution-record rules, package flags, scope exclusion, coverage figures and the §6 verdict. Every reference value was computed by functionaltest-ref.py, an independent standard-library re-implementation of the spec written without the tool code, and asserted against a hand-derived expectation per check. Phase vocabulary and test purpose follow IEC 62381:2024 (FAT/FIT/SAT/SIT), IEC 62382:2024 (loop check between loop construction and cold commissioning, documented per cl. 7) and IEC 61511-1:2016 cl. 15 (SIS safety validation against the SRS); the five-point injection, tolerance rule, voting combinations, bypass-restoration and proof-test predicates are the spec's author method.
reference_citations: IEC 62382:2024 Ed. 3.0 'Control systems in the process industry - Electrical and instrumentation loop check', preview sample https://cdn.standards.iteh.ai/samples/104569/954e455763a94f98b5f16dce4ef31098/IEC-62382-2024.pdf - 1.1 scope, 3.1.15 loop, clause titles 4-10 incl. 7 'Documentation of performed loop checks' (read 2026-09-22)

IEC 62381:2024 Ed. 3.0 'Automation systems in the process industry - FAT, SAT and SIT', webstore listing and preview sample as cited in spec §0 (clauses 5-8, 3.1.16 punch list); not re-read beyond the spec's quotation

IEC 61511-1:2016 cl. 15 SIS safety validation, 15.1.1 objective as quoted by Emerson Automation Experts 'Safety Validation in the IEC 61511 Process Safety Lifecycle' (2010) https://www.emersonautomationexperts.com/2010/safety/safety_validati/ (read 2026-09-22); the standard's 15.2 item list was not read
FNV-1a 32-bit parameters (offset basis 2166136261, prime 16777619) and check vectors '' -> 811c9dc5, 'a' -> e40c292c as given in spec §4.4
tolerance: Categorical, boolean, integer, id-list and hash checks are exact (discrete logic; any deviation is a logic difference). `test.<id>.expected` is compared as canonical JSON (spec §4.4). Coverage percentages are one IEEE division: relative 1e-12. Loop expected values, deviations and signals are at most three IEEE operations in the spec's expression order: relative 1e-12, and absolute 1e-9·S (S = span) where the reference is exactly 0, as spec §13.2 states. Every `within` check keeps ||d| - t| > 1e-6·S so no floating boundary decides it; the exact-equality boundary |d| = t is checked only through rule_absent.

not_benchmarked: Step, precondition, label and expected_text wording, and the seven-language UI (spec §14).
UI behaviour: conflict table, filters, figures, mobile layout, permalink size fallback, PDF layout (spec §14).
Package transport (explicit load, round trip, ignored-field report, atomic refusal of save while FUN-R-007 fires) and §7.2 field aliases: package cases per TZ-project-package §7, not this corpus.
'Refresh from model' and idempotent re-generation (acceptance 3 and 9): actions on a state, not expressible in the §13.1 input vocabulary.
Display-unit conversions (§4.8) and the 0-10V signal value (§13.2 names only signal_A).
Generation-refusal input limits of §2 (20 matrices, 2 000 cells, 5 000 tests ...): no case exceeds them except n = 9 channels, see vote-n9-single.
Segment classes of Figure 1 (valid_pass / fail / invalid_pass / deferred / not_tested / no_test): not a §13.2 checkable key.
Hashes of strings outside the Basic Multilingual Plane (spec §14).
The content of IEC 61511-1:2016 15.2 and IEC 62382 test-point percentages or tolerances: not read (spec §0); the corresponding rules are the spec's author method.
coverage: 128 cases (113 authored + 4 added by the first adjudication 2026-09-23 + 11 added by the second adjudication 2026-09-23). Rules with a triggering case: 34 of 34 (all). Rules with a near-miss case where they do not fire: 34 of 34 (all). Headline claims: presets P1-P4 with spec §9 findings, coverage and verdicts; §4.4 worked hashes; acceptance 4 (setpoint change stales exactly the cause's tests), 5 (non-slice edits stale nothing), 7 (boundaries |d| = t and tolerance = accuracy), 8 (voting counts 0/3/6/7, 255 at n = 8, FUN-R-008 at n = 9). Added by the first adjudication: §5.5 loop span taken from the range recorded in the test after a model change, §5.3 hidden test of an excluded category firing nothing, §4.3 unconditional reset step of a generated sif_proof, §5.5 suppression of FUN-R-042 while FUN-R-043 fires. Added by the second adjudication: the §4.7 valid-pass list against a pass that fires FUN-R-043, the §4.5 required checkpoint set (short list, empty list), the loop rules that read the point and not the stored expected (FUN-R-041, -043, -044), FUN-R-043 without an upper tolerance bound, the control_function branch of FUN-R-052, the effects[].tag branch of FUN-R-004, the coverage denominator of two sources sharing one key (transitions and io), and the 'one finding per (rule, target)' sentence of §5.
